project: Document Factory Validation as the Pre-Run Gate
description: Add a canonical packaged Factory-validation guide that makes `you factory config validate` the required static gate before first run, documents its current checks and exact file/directory invocations, demonstrates the real unsupported three-input join diagnostic, and integrates validation into the Factory authoring workflow without changing product behavior.

context.customerAsk: Document `you factory config validate` as the pre-run static gate now that it catches unsupported join arity. Explain schema validation, supported join arity, guard cardinality and references, split-layout `AGENTS.md` requirements, and classifier route validity; give exact file and directory invocations; include a worked failing arity example with the real diagnostic; wire validation before first run; keep canonical content in `docs/reference/`; execute every shown CLI command against the current binary; run the named behavioral regression, `make docs-reference-smoke`, and `make verify-fast`; respect the D4 cut list; and deliver through actual PR merge.
context.problem: Validation is mentioned across existing references but is not presented as one required pre-run gate, has no dedicated packaged topic, and lacks a worked unsupported-join diagnostic. Factory authors can therefore reach runtime with preventable schema or topology defects and mistake an unsupported join for a runtime stall.
context.solution: Publish `you docs factory-validation` from canonical reference Markdown, accurately describe the current validate-only contract and its limits, show exact portable-file and split-directory commands, include a current-binary three-input SAME_NAME plus ALL_CHILDREN_COMPLETE failure and remediation, and update the canonical authoring workflow to require validation until passing before first run and after relevant authored changes.

acceptanceCriteria: `you docs factory-validation` returns a canonical packaged reference topic that identifies `you factory config validate` as the required static gate before a Factory's first run and distinguishes validation from execution, persistence, provider calls, and a guarantee of runtime success.

The guide gives exact portable-file and split-directory invocation forms and accurately explains current checks for schema/definition validity, unsupported join arity, guard cardinality and referenced inputs, split-layout worker/workstation `AGENTS.md` requirements, and classifier labels/routes.

A worked invalid three-input SAME_NAME plus ALL_CHILDREN_COMPLETE Factory is rejected before runtime, and the documented current-binary diagnostic states that the observed arity is 3, at most 2 inputs are supported, and the author can split the fan-in into supported two-input stages or reduce its inputs.

The canonical authoring workflow requires validation after authoring or changing a Factory and immediately before first run, while root docs remain routing material and no unrelated docs, runtime, API, UI, OpenAPI, or generated-client behavior changes.

During implementation, every CLI invocation shown in new or changed documentation is executed against the current built `you` binary; its actual output is pasted where instructional or asserted in direct behavioral/docs smoke evidence, and no undocumented flag or invented output remains.

Quality gates pass: `go test ./tests/functional/factory_definitions/transports/cli/validate_persist -run 'TestFactoryValidate(RejectsUnsupportedJoinArity|AcceptsSupportedTwoInputJoinArity)$' -count=1`, `make docs-reference-smoke`, and `make verify-fast`; Typecheck passes; Tests pass; no NEW lint violations relative to current main, and the gates green on main (backend-size, pkg-maint, pkg-file-count, pkg-structure, vet) stay green.

Delivery continues through implementation and review until required CI is terminal and passing, all blocking PR conversation feedback is explicitly addressed, merge conflicts and shared-file/current-main changes are reconciled, and the PR is actually merged; opened, green, approved, or ready-to-merge is not complete.

userStories.title: Publish the packaged pre-run validation guide
userStories.description: As a Factory author, I want one discoverable packaged validation guide so I can check an authored Factory with the correct command and understand what the static gate does before I run it.
acceptanceCriteria: `you docs factory-validation` renders the new canonical topic through the packaged docs surface and the docs index routes readers to it with a concise validation-focused description.

The guide states that `you factory config validate` is the required static gate before first run and validates without starting a Factory Session, invoking a provider, or persisting the submitted Factory.
The guide shows exact current syntax for a portable JSON/YAML file and for a split Factory directory containing exactly one supported Factory definition file.

The guide explains in author-facing terms that validation covers document/schema and definition errors, supported join arity, workstation and per-input guard cardinality/references, required split-layout worker/workstation `AGENTS.md` content, and classifier route labels/outputs.
The guide states that a pass accepts the current static contract but does not guarantee provider readiness, external resources, runtime liveness, or successful execution.
Every CLI invocation added by this story is executed against the current built binary, and its real output is pasted where instructional or asserted by direct packaged-docs evidence.
`make docs-reference-smoke` passes.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Implemented the canonical packaged factory-validation topic, embedded and registered it, routed it from the root/reference indexes, and added packaged-topic smoke coverage. Rebuilt bin/you.exe and executed every CLI invocation shown by the guide: the six related docs topics and the portable JSON, portable YAML, and split-directory validation commands all exited 0 with the documented output. Verified with make docs-reference-smoke, the named unsupported-join regression, and make verify-fast (after make ui-deps).

userStories.title: Show the real unsupported-join failure and correction
userStories.description: As a Factory author diagnosing a fan-in, I want a worked failing example with the real arity diagnostic so I can correct an unsupported topology before it becomes a silent runtime stall.
acceptanceCriteria: The guide includes a minimal internally coherent Factory whose workstation has three inputs combined through SAME_NAME and ALL_CHILDREN_COMPLETE, matching the unsupported A3 join shape.
Running the exact documented validation invocation against that example with the current built binary fails before a Factory Session or provider execution begins.

The worked output is copied from the current binary and identifies the affected workstation, the unsupported SAME_NAME plus ALL_CHILDREN_COMPLETE join, observed arity of 3 inputs, and supported maximum of 2 inputs; no diagnostic wording, status, or flag is invented.
The guide directs the author to reduce the joined inputs or split the fan-in into supported two-input workstation stages and then validate the corrected Factory again before running it.

`go test ./tests/functional/factory_definitions/transports/cli/validate_persist -run 'TestFactoryValidate(RejectsUnsupportedJoinArity|AcceptsSupportedTwoInputJoinArity)$' -count=1` passes and directly proves both the unsupported rejection and supported two-input boundary.
Every CLI invocation added by this story is executed against the current built binary, with actual output pasted in the guide or asserted by direct behavioral evidence.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Added reproducible unsupported three-input and supported two-input join fixtures under docs/examples/factory-validation and documented the worked failure/correction in the packaged guide. Rebuilt bin/you.exe and executed both exact validation commands; pasted the current binary output, including the structured blocking target and exit behavior. Verified with the named unsupported-join regression, make docs-reference-smoke, and make verify-fast (typecheck, UI/Bun tests, MCP contract check, and short Go suite).

userStories.title: Require validation in the Factory authoring workflow
userStories.description: As a Factory author following the main authoring guide, I want validation placed immediately before first execution so invalid definitions are corrected before runtime scheduling starts.
acceptanceCriteria: The canonical workflow sequences author or change the Factory, run `you factory config validate` on the authored file or directory, correct all blocking findings, validate again until it passes, and only then perform the first run.
Existing validation guidance routes to `you docs factory-validation` for detailed checks and the worked failure instead of duplicating another long guide outside the canonical topic.
The workflow requires validation again after later topology, guard, route, schema, or split-layout prompt/configuration changes and before the next run that relies on those changes.

Root documentation stays concise routing/index material, and the diff contains no local-model harness, llama-server trace testing, Gemma validation, ACP expansion, wrapper-layer multimodal transformation, storage engine, runtime behavior, API contract, or frontend behavior.
Every CLI invocation introduced or changed in workflow passages is executed against the current built binary, with real output pasted where instructional or asserted by packaged-docs smoke evidence.
`make docs-reference-smoke` and `make verify-fast` pass.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
